subtopic: Physical Properties of Aldehydes and Ketones
stem:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of their boiling points:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\), \(\text{H}_5\text{C}_2\text{-O-C}_2\text{H}_5\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
solution:
The molecular masses of these compounds are in the range of 72 to 74. Since only butan-1-ol molecules are associated due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, therefore, the boiling point of butan-1-ol would be the highest. Butanal is more polar than ethoxyethane. Therefore, the intermolecular dipole-dipole attraction is stronger in the former. \(n\)-Pentane molecules have only weak van der Waals forces. Hence increasing order of boiling points of the given compounds is as follows:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 < \text{H}_5\text{C}_2\text{-O-C}_2\text{H}_5 < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} < \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\)
_note: BOOK INCONSISTENCY, transcribed faithfully: the stem's fourth compound is printed CH3CH2CH2CH3 (n-butane, M = 58), verified at 3x zoom, yet the printed solution says the molecular masses are 'in the range of 72 to 74' and calls that compound 'n-Pentane'. The intended compound is evidently n-pentane, CH3CH2CH2CH2CH3 (M = 72). The stated order is unaffected either way.

subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
stem: Would you expect benzaldehyde to be more reactive or less reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions than propanal? Explain your answer.
solution: The carbon atom of the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde is less electrophilic than carbon atom of the carbonyl group present in propanal. The polarity of the carbonyl group is reduced in benzaldehyde due to resonance with the benzene ring (the ring donates electron density into the carbonyl group, generating a resonance structure carrying a positive charge on the ring and a negative charge on oxygen), and hence it is less reactive than propanal.

subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
stem: An organic compound (A) with molecular formula \(\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}\) forms an orange-red precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and gives yellow precipitate on heating with iodine in the presence of sodium hydroxide. It neither reduces Tollens' or Fehlings' reagent, nor does it decolourise bromine water or Baeyer's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, it gives a carboxylic acid (B) having molecular formula \(\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2\). Identify the compounds (A) and (B) and explain the reactions involved.
solution:
(A) forms 2,4-DNP derivative. Therefore, it is an aldehyde or a ketone. Since it does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling reagent, (A) must be a ketone. (A) responds to iodoform test. Therefore, it should be a methyl ketone. The molecular formula of (A) indicates high degree of unsaturation, yet it does not decolourise bromine water or Baeyer's reagent. This indicates the presence of unsaturation due to an aromatic ring.

Compound (B), being an oxidation product of a ketone should be a carboxylic acid. The molecular formula of (B) indicates that it should be benzoic acid and compound (A) should, therefore, be a monosubstituted aromatic methyl ketone. The molecular formula of (A) indicates that it should be phenyl methyl ketone (acetophenone). Reactions are as follows:

\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3\) (A) \(+\ \text{H}_2\text{NNHC}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2 \xrightarrow{-\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{=N-NHC}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2\) (2,4-DNP derivative)

\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{I}_2]{\text{NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} + \text{CHI}_3\)

\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{CrO}_4} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\) (B), \(\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2\)
_note: The book's printed solution ends with three drawn reaction schemes, the last two of which are set on the following page (p-14); all three are transcribed here as equations.

subtopic: Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids
stem:
Write chemical reactions to affect the following transformations:
(i) Butan-1-ol to butanoic acid
(ii) Benzyl alcohol to phenylethanoic acid
(iii) 3-Nitrobromobenzene to 3-nitrobenzoic acid
(iv) 4-Methylacetophenone to benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid
(v) Cyclohexene to hexane-1,6-dioic acid
(vi) Butanal to butanoic acid.
solution:
(i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow[\text{Jones reagent}]{\text{CrO}_3\text{-H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (butan-1-ol to butanoic acid)

(ii) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{HBr}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CN} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (phenylethanoic acid)

(iii) 3-Nitrobromobenzene \(\xrightarrow[\text{ether}]{\text{Mg}}\) 3-nitrophenylmagnesium bromide \(\xrightarrow{\text{CO}_2\ (\text{dry ice})}\) the carboxylate \(\text{-COOMgBr}\) \(\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}}\) 3-nitrobenzoic acid

(iv) 4-Methylacetophenone \(\xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4/\text{KOH}}\) dipotassium benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate \(\xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4}\) benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid)

(v) Cyclohexene \(\xrightarrow[\text{Heat}]{\text{KMnO}_4\text{-H}_2\text{SO}_4}\) \(\text{HOOC}(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}\), hexane-1,6-dioic acid (adipic acid)

(vi) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow[\text{(Tollens' reagent)}]{\text{Ammoniacal AgNO}_3} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}\) (butanoic acid)
_note: The book prints this solution as six drawn reaction schemes on the following page (p-21); transcribed here as equations. In (iii) the Grignard route is drawn on the ring.
